teams.heading: Jake White's 35-man Fiji squad includes ex-England Nathan Hughes, four uncapped players
teams.body: Ex-England back Nathan Hughes, who won 22 caps between 2016 and 2019, is in Fiji's squad after being drafted into Jake White's 35-man group for the November Nations Championship block. He is one of four uncapped players, alongside Peniami Narisia, Marika Parker and Setareki Bituniyata, and White could give the other three their first Test caps this month. Fiji come in off a 34-28 win over Japan and face France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the shortlist and concerns Fiji's own squad, which is the most useful story for a fan ahead of the November block.

teams.heading: Kepu Tuipulotu a doubt for England's autumn Tests with knee injury
teams.body: Hooker Kepu Tuipulotu has emerged as a doubt for England's Nations Championship campaign after picking up a knee injury in national training on Tuesday. The uncapped 21-year-old had been tipped to make his England breakthrough this autumn, and it is understood he will not be in the squad for the opener with Australia, with the timeframe for his return unclear. Fin Smith is a major doubt for the Wallabies fixture. He joined Bath's academy in 2024 and signed a contract to 2028 earlier this year.

lead.why: It is the strongest new England men's story in the pack, a hooker's knee injury that puts an uncapped breakthrough player's autumn in doubt.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards joins Argentina's Pumas, reportedly ruling out Borthwick role
teams.body: Defence coach Shaun Edwards has joined Argentina's Pumas for a Rugby World Cup push in Australia, a move AP reported on 23 October. Coverage says the switch rules out any role in Steve Borthwick's England set-up, closing off the route reported earlier this month. The Daily Mail's view was that Steve Borthwick and the RFU had missed a golden opportunity.

teams.heading: Joey Carbery impresses as Leinster rout Connacht 50-5 in URC
teams.body: Joey Carbery kicked from the tee and in open play, scored a try and converted it from the touchline, and Planet Rugby called him the visitors' 'biggest attacking weapon' as Leinster beat Connacht 50-5 in the URC on Friday evening. Tries from Gus McCarthy, Jordan Larmour and Todd Lawlor had Leinster well clear inside the first half-hour, and Dave Heffernan supplied Connacht's only response. Planet Rugby also credited a 'ferocious' Leinster defence that left the hosts with little cohesive attack.

lead.why: It is the strongest genuinely new item in the pack about an Ireland player's form, and the other new items are either Argentina's squad, women's rugby, or the Fiji 'A' squad already reported.

teams.heading: Italy U18 technical director Alessandro Lodi names side for Ireland test
teams.body: Italy Under 18 head to Badia Polesine on Saturday for a test against Ireland's Under 18s, and technical director Alessandro Lodi has named his side. The match comes a year after Italy beat Ireland 54-14 in Cosenza, and Lodi says he expects an intense game with high tempo and heavy pressure. He wants his players to show courage and personality, and to keep their own style of play.

lead.why: The only new Italy-side item in the pack, and it is a team announcement, which beats the already-reported Quesada squad stories.

teams.heading: Duhan van der Merwe released from Scotland squad to play for Edinburgh
teams.body: Duhan van der Merwe has been released from Scotland's squad to return to Edinburgh for Saturday's URC match against Benetton, with Gregor Townsend wanting the winger to build match fitness. It is not a punishment, the Scotland boss stressing it is not a sign the winger has fallen out of favour. Van der Merwe has played just 18 minutes this season, his comeback against the Lions cut short by a dislocated finger. Townsend said: "It was a much better outcome than it looked at the time."

lead.why: A Scotland squad decision about a named player that the edition hasn't led on before, while the Glasgow match and Russell pieces have already run.

teams.heading: Wales release Josh Adams to play for Cardiff against Ospreys
teams.body: Wales have released wing Josh Adams to play for Cardiff in Saturday's Welsh derby against the Ospreys, giving the 31-year-old more game time. He has played only twice this season, returning earlier this month off the bench against Northampton Saints. Last year he was a regular for Wales, starting two autumn Tests and every Six Nations match, plus two summer games. Cardiff, beaten at the Arms Park by the Sharks last Friday, will be looking to bounce back.

lead.why: It is the only men's Wales squad story on the shortlist, and the rest are either already reported, women's rugby or a club item.

teams.heading: Contepomi recalls Facundo Isa for Ireland opener, replacing injured Santiago Grondona
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi has finalised his first Nations Championship squad, and the headline call is the return of veteran Facundo Isa, who replaces the injured Santiago Grondona. Isa's last Argentina appearance came in July 2025, and he missed out on international duty in 2024 and 2026. The 33-man group travels to Dublin for the opener against Ireland, while Franco Molina, a mainstay in Contepomi selections, misses out and Tomás Lavanini returns in the second row.

lead.why: A new squad story about Argentina's own players, with the recall of Facundo Isa as the headline call, and it is not the already-covered England A roster.

teams.heading: Les Kiss says Kurtley Beale is in consideration for World Cup squad
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss says Kurtley Beale is in consideration for Australia’s Rugby World Cup squad, and insists the 95-cap veteran is “in there to perform”. Beale was added to the spring tour squad after Hunter Paisami withdrew for personal reasons, and Kiss says feedback from Force figures Nic White, Simon Cron and Brad Harris has been positive. The coach will reassess his No. 10 options after the next Super Rugby Pacific season.

lead.why: The freshest item on the shortlist with a new angle: Kiss on Beale's World Cup chances, not the recall already run.

teams.heading: Japan's Nations Championship: 62 points scored, 88 conceded in three matches
teams.body: Japan have won one of their three Nations Championship matches, and sit 10th of 12 in the log. Across those three games they have scored 62 points and conceded 88, a points difference of -26. Their most recent result was a 28-34 defeat to Fiji, and Wales are next, in Round 4. Japan's highest world ranking is No. 7, reached in 2019.

teams.heading: Patrick Tuipulotu and Sam Darry omitted from All Blacks' northern tour squad
teams.body: Patrick Tuipulotu and Sam Darry are both left out of the 36-man squad for the November tour to Scotland, Wales and England, with Jamie Hannah picked ahead of them. Darry started two Tests in Rugby's Greatest Rivalry and had a strong Nations Championship, yet has drifted down the second-row pecking order. Stephen Donald said Dave Rennie has quickly built depth, adding that Darry is unlucky and that some players now genuinely miss out. Du'Plessis Kirifi and Kyren Taumoefolau also miss out.

lead.why: It is a squad story with named players and a concrete omission, and it is fresher and more fan-relevant than the pundit column or the selection-policy item.

teams.heading: Beast Mtawarira credits Matthew Proudfoot for making Springbok scrum a real weapon
teams.body: Beast Mtawarira has credited former Springboks scrum coach Matthew Proudfoot for moving the scrum from a place where South Africa sought ascendancy to one where they want to inflict pain on opponents. Speaking on the Squidge Rugby YouTube channel, he said the culture really started evolving in 2018. He added that the calibre and depth of the props have contributed too. He also praised the current scrum coach: "Daan Human is a fantastic coach and built on what Matthew Proudfoot set back in 2018."

lead.why: The Marx item is a headline-only report that cannot support a 55-word body, while the Mtawarira interview gives a sourced South Africa angle on the scrum.
